adjudication.diagnosis_label: Acute appendicitis, uncomplicated (CT-confirmed) — Alvarado 10/10 (very probable), AIR 6/12 (intermediate probability); the two scores disagree and the disagreement is adjudicated, below

evidence_chain.role: Migration 1 + anorexia 1 + nausea/vomiting 1 + RIF tenderness 2 + rebound 1 + temperature 1 + leukocytosis 2 + left shift 1 = 10/10, 'very probable' (C17). Partial at stage 1: 7 points with leukocytosis and shift not-assessed.

Vomiting 1 + RIF pain 1 + rebound light 1 + temperature 0 (37.6 < 38.5) + PMN 70-84% 1 + WBC 10-14.9 1 + CRP 10-49 1 = 6/12, 'intermediate probability' (C18). Partial at stage 1: 3 points with wbc, pmn and crp not-assessed.

Migration of pain LR+ 3.18 (C19) moves the workbench board's appendicitis mass from the 0.33 prior to 0.61 at stage 1 — strong, but short of commitment, which is exactly the intermediate zone the AIR score also reports.

Negative urine beta-hCG, LR- 0.0361 (C21), retires hyp.ectopic-pregnancy at stage 2 (workbench posterior 0.0022, below the 0.02 rule-out threshold) — the stage ordering is the lesson: the history raised the hypothesis at stage 1 and the cheapest test in the pathway retired it at stage 2.

Normal ovaries with preserved Doppler flow, no mass, no free fluid (f.us-ovaries-normal, f.us-no-free-fluid): the gynaecological exclusions' imaging legs. The appendix was not visualised (f.us-appendix-not-visualized) — recorded as a non-result with no LR taken.

Dilated 11 mm appendix, wall thickening, fat stranding, appendicolith: LR+ 16.421 computed from C19's cited CT accuracy pair. The workbench board's appendicitis mass reaches 0.97 at stage 4 and every rival falls below 0.02 for the first time.
No perforation, no abscess, no free gas, no generalised contamination: the case dispositions to the Theatre procedure's standard configuration, not its perforated branch (management.handoff).

excluded.basis: Negative urine beta-hCG (f.hcg-negative; LR- 0.0361, C21 — workbench posterior 0.0022, ruled out at stage 2), PLUS no adnexal mass and no free fluid on ultrasound (f.us-ovaries-normal, f.us-no-free-fluid) and unremarkable adnexa on CT (f.ct-rest-normal). The exclusion is stated as the conjunction because a small minority of ectopic pregnancies test negative; the test alone is not presented as absolute.

Both ovaries normal in size and appearance with preserved arterial and venous Doppler flow on ultrasound (f.us-ovaries-normal) and unremarkable adnexa on CT (f.ct-rest-normal), in a 24-hour constant-pain presentation with an established alternative diagnosis. Recorded honestly: preserved Doppler flow alone does not exclude torsion — the exclusion is the conjunction of two normal imaging studies, no mass, and the confirmed appendix pathology; the disposition operation is laparoscopic, so the adnexa are inspected at surgery in any case.

No ovarian cyst is seen on either study (f.us-ovaries-normal, f.ct-rest-normal) and there is no free fluid anywhere (f.us-no-free-fluid, f.ct-rest-normal) — a ruptured cyst that produces this presentation leaves a cyst, fluid, or both.

No urinary symptoms (f.no-urinary-symptoms), no costovertebral angle tenderness (f.no-flank-pain), a clear urinalysis (f.ua-clear), and pain that migrated periumbilical-to-RIF rather than sitting in the flank; fever is low-grade (37.6 C). Qualitative exclusion — no LR for these absences was consulted.

Pain constant and migratory, not colicky, with no groin radiation (f.no-flank-pain); no haematuria on urinalysis (f.ua-clear); CT shows no ureteric calculus and no hydronephrosis (f.ct-rest-normal) and shows the appendix instead.
No discharge, no cervical motion tenderness, no adnexal tenderness or mass (f.no-pid-features); negative pregnancy test; normal adnexa on two imaging studies; and a confirmed alternative diagnosis.

Excluded by the positive CT diagnosis: the imaged appendix pathology is a complete explanation of the presentation, and no finding in the case points elsewhere (no diarrhoea for gastroenteritis, no colicky pain for a stone, no urinary findings).

adjudication.note: How the case's three quantitative instruments divide the work, stated so none is mistaken for another: the WORKBENCH BOARD moves only on the three sourced likelihood ratios (migration 3.18, negative hCG 0.0361, CT 16.421) and exists to teach staged probability revision with an auditable rule; the two SCORE BLOCKS are computed mechanically from the findings by the same machinery that computes TG18-style criteria, and exist to teach what each instrument prices; neither score is multiplied into the board, and no composite of any kind is formed — the checker asserts the absence of composite keys across the case and debrief JSON, as in cases 1 and 2.

score_comparison.agreement: Both instruments rank appendicitis first among the named hypotheses, both are built from the same bedside evidence, and both complete only when the stage-2 bloods arrive — at stage 1 each is a partial total with its unmeasured items recorded not-assessed, never assumed.
score_comparison.disagreement: They place the patient in different risk classes, and the case is built so the divergence is mechanical, not impressionistic. Alvarado saturates: it prices presence, not magnitude — tenderness is worth 2 points at any severity, leukocytosis 2 points at any count above 10.0, and its temperature line (37.3 C) is low enough that 37.6 C scores. This patient's soft values (WBC 12.4, neutrophils 78%, temperature 37.6 C, light rebound) therefore max it out at 10/10. AIR prices magnitude: the same values land in its lowest positive bands (WBC 10-14.9 = 1 of 2; PMN 70-84% = 1 of 2; CRP 10-49 = 1 of 2; rebound light = 1 of 3), its temperature line (38.5 C) is not met, and it totals 6/12, intermediate. The guideline evidence consulted for this case (C20) sides with AIR's caution twice over: the Alvarado score is not sufficiently specific to positively confirm appendicitis in adults (statement 1.3), AIR is among the best-performing scores (statement 1.4), and intermediate-risk patients — women of reproductive age in particular — go to imaging rather than straight to theatre. The CT was therefore not a formality after a 10/10: it was the adjudicating evidence the better-calibrated instrument called for, and it also carried the severity information (uncomplicated, standard position) that selected the Theatre branch.
score_comparison.teaching_point: A score is a measuring instrument with a calibration, not a verdict. When two validated instruments disagree, the disagreement itself is information about which features each one prices — here, presence versus magnitude — and the pathway follows the instrument whose calibration the evidence supports, with imaging as the tiebreaker the guideline prescribes.

available_tests.name: Full blood count with differential
available_tests.note: Settles four score items across both instruments (Alvarado leukocytosis and left shift; AIR white count and neutrophil proportion) — the machinery therefore classifies it criteria-completing, and the classification is the lesson: in a score-driven pathway a blood count completes criteria rather than discriminating on its own.

available_tests.name: C-reactive protein
available_tests.note: Settles the AIR score's CRP item. The Alvarado score (1986) predates routine CRP and contains no CRP item — one structural reason the two instruments can disagree.

available_tests.name: Urine beta-hCG (pregnancy test)
available_tests.note: The case's decisive stage-ordered test: the workup discipline for abdominal pain in a woman of childbearing age requires it (C19), and its negative likelihood ratio (C21) retires the ectopic-pregnancy hypothesis at stage 2. The machinery classifies it discriminating (its LR crosses the rule-out threshold) rather than merely a safety net.

available_tests.name: Urinalysis (dipstick and microscopy)
available_tests.note: The urinary safety net: a clear urinalysis is the laboratory leg of the exclusions of pyelonephritis and ureteric stone. Qualitative only — no LR for these findings was consulted.

available_tests.name: Pelvic and transabdominal ultrasound
available_tests.note: In this pathway the ultrasound's job is the gynaecological must-not-miss set (C19: pelvic ultrasound to assess torsion, symptomatic cysts, ectopic pregnancy). Its appendix yield is honestly a non-result: the appendix was not visualised, and no LR is taken from that.

available_tests.name: CT abdomen and pelvis with IV contrast
available_tests.note: The adjudicating study, reached because the AIR score left the patient intermediate-risk and the guideline pathway for intermediate-risk patients — and for women of reproductive age — is imaging (C20), not because the Alvarado score's high total demanded confirmation. Its composite positive carries the case's only imaging LR (C19).

Last menstrual period 3 weeks ago, regular 28-day cycles; sexually active; no hormonal contraception; no prior ectopic pregnancy, pelvic inflammatory disease, or abdominal surgery (case data). ABSENT finding, recorded explicitly: no dysuria, no urinary frequency or urgency, no visible haematuria (case data). The history leg of the exclusions of pyelonephritis and ureteric stone; the laboratory leg is f.ua-clear at stage 2.

Recorded at stage 1 because it is severity evidence: it is consistent with the uncomplicated course the CT later confirms, and it is why the AIR rebound grade is light rather than medium or strong.

findings.lr_note: No standalone LR for the white cell count is applied: the consulted meta-analytic literature (C19's lineage) treats the inflammatory variables as strongest in combination, and the scores are where this case prices them — multiplying a per-variable LR on top of the same variables' score points would double-count one evidence stream.
findings.text: White cell count elevated at 12.4 x10^9/L (reference 4.5-11.0, C7). Priced three ways by the scores, all stated: above the Alvarado leukocytosis line of 10.0 (2 points, C17); inside the AIR band 10.0-14.9 (1 point, C18).

criteria_roles: Alvarado item: left shift, segmented neutrophils > 75% (C17)
findings.text: Segmented neutrophils 78% of the differential (case data). Above the Alvarado left-shift line of > 75% segmented neutrophils (1 point, C17); inside the AIR band 70-84% (1 point, C18).

C-reactive protein 26 mg/L (case data) — inside the AIR band 10-49 mg/L (1 point, C18), and above the 10 mg/L inflammatory-response threshold the TG18 lineage uses (C2). The Alvarado score contains no CRP item (C17) — one of the structural reasons the two scores diverge on this patient.

lr.computed_from: C21 sensitivity 0.97, specificity 0.83 for ectopic pregnancy: LR- = (1 - 0.97) / 0.83 = 0.0361
lr.note: Single study (C21: urine test for intact hCG and free beta-hCG in early-pregnancy presentations; NPV 99.3% in that cohort) — labelled single-study wherever used. The residual caveat is part of this finding's record: a small minority of ectopic pregnancies test negative, so the adjudication's exclusion of ectopic pregnancy rests on this test PLUS two normal adnexal imaging studies, not on the test alone.

findings.text: Urine beta-hCG NEGATIVE (case data) — the case's decisive stage-ordered finding: the pregnancy test the workup discipline requires in a woman of childbearing age (C19) returns at stage 2, after the history (f.lmp-history) has made ectopic pregnancy a live hypothesis.

Urinalysis clear (case data): no pyuria, no nitrites, no haematuria on dipstick and microscopy. The laboratory leg of the exclusions of pyelonephritis and ureteric stone; unquantified — no LR for urinalysis findings in this presentation was consulted, and none is invented.

findings.lr_note: Deliberately unquantified — see the finding text. The appendix question passes to CT untouched by this study.
findings.text: Ultrasound (transabdominal and pelvic, case imaging report): the appendix is NOT visualised. Recorded as a non-result, in those terms: non-visualisation is not a negative examination, and no likelihood ratio is taken from it — the accuracy figures in C19 describe examinations in which the appendix is assessed, and a non-visualised appendix is neither a positive nor a negative of that kind.

Ultrasound (case imaging report): both ovaries are normal in size and appearance, with preserved arterial and venous Doppler flow bilaterally; no adnexal mass and no ovarian cyst is seen. The imaging leg of the exclusions of ovarian torsion and ruptured ovarian cyst — qualitative: no LR for a normal pelvic ultrasound against torsion was consulted. The case records the standard caution as part of the exclusion's basis (adjudication): preserved Doppler flow alone does not exclude torsion; the exclusion is the conjunction of normal morphology on two modalities, no mass, no free fluid, and an established alternative diagnosis.

ABSENT finding, recorded explicitly: no free fluid in the pouch of Douglas or elsewhere in the pelvis or abdomen on ultrasound (case data). Against ruptured ovarian cyst and ruptured ectopic pregnancy, qualitatively — a rupture that bleeds leaves fluid, and there is none.

lr.computed_from: C19 sensitivity 0.936, specificity 0.943 (Kinner et al. CT comparison, as reported in C19): LR+ = 0.936 / (1 - 0.943) = 16.421
lr.note: The accuracy pair comes from a children-and-young-adults comparison (C19); this patient is 26. The derivation is labelled with that population wherever it is used.

findings.text: CT abdomen and pelvis with IV contrast (case imaging report): the appendix is dilated at 11 mm with mural thickening and enhancement, periappendiceal fat stranding, and an appendicolith; it arises from the caecal pole and lies in standard position in the right iliac fossa. This composite — not any single sign — is the result the consulted CT accuracy figures (C19) describe.

CT (case imaging report): NO perforation, NO periappendiceal abscess or collection, NO free intraperitoneal gas, and NO generalised contamination (case data — the absences are recorded findings, not defaults). This finding is what places the case on the Theatre procedure's standard configuration rather than its perforated severity branch (see management.handoff).

CT, remainder of the study (case imaging report): the adnexa are unremarkable bilaterally; there is no ureteric calculus, no hydronephrosis, and no free fluid. The cross-sectional corroboration of the ultrasound's gynaecological exclusions, and the imaging leg of the ureteric-stone exclusion.

ground_truth.diagnosis: Acute appendicitis, uncomplicated — CT-confirmed; Alvarado 10/10 (very probable) and AIR 6/12 (intermediate probability) disagree, and the adjudication derives the disposition from the disagreement rather than from either number alone

Case 3's imaging link is therefore localisation-by-neighbour (the colon/caecum label), and the appendix anatomy the learner manipulates in the Theatre comes from the Body Model, not from s0778.

imaging_link.honesty_block: Three different individuals are in play and the case keeps them separate: the synthetic patient (a 26-year-old woman, authored case data); imaging subject s0778 (a 57-year-old MAN's CT — different person, different sex, different scan); and the atlas individual behind the Body Model geometry. No co-registration between any of them is claimed or implied. The s0778 series does NOT show the appendix — its shipped label set has no appendix label at all — and it does not show this case's pathology: there are no labels for wall thickening, fat stranding or an appendicolith, so the case's CT findings (f.ct-appendicitis and companions) are authored case data from a fictional scanner encounter, labelled case-data at every appearance. What the link DOES establish, mechanically, is the same thing case 1's link established: the crosswalk's colon label exists, its counted extent is re-verified by the checker from the shipped bins at every run, and the label's caudal reach covers the caecal region this case is about.

management.alternatives_considered: An antibiotics-first, non-operative strategy for uncomplicated appendicitis is a live topic in the consulted guideline's surgical section (C20), and in a real service it would be discussed with the patient. This case's disposition is operative by design — the workbench's purpose here is the case-to-Theatre loop — and the alternative is recorded rather than silently omitted.
management.disposition: Admit to the surgical service. IV fluids, analgesia, antiemetic, nil by mouth; a preoperative broad-spectrum antibiotic dose per the treating team's protocol (supportive specifics are case data, not guideline quotation). Definitive treatment is operative: early laparoscopic appendicectomy, handed to the Theatre module below.

handoff.basis: CT-adjudicated UNCOMPLICATED appendicitis with the appendix in standard position: f.ct-uncomplicated records no perforation, no abscess, no free gas and no generalised contamination, and f.ct-appendicitis places the appendix at the caecal pole in the right iliac fossa. The disposition is therefore the procedure's standard configuration (36 required microsteps — the configuration Milestone 28's trace-06 runs clean, PASS 37/37). The perforated severity branch (trace-09) is NOT invoked, because its trigger findings are absent — and the absences are recorded findings in this case file, not assumptions. Neither variant configuration (retrocecal, pelvic) is invoked: the appendix was imaged in standard position. The CT describes a non-necrotic base, so the trace-06 closure decision (endoloop on a healthy base, procedure decision point dp3) is the branch the case implies; the necrotic-base/stapler branch and its stump-leak consequence are not entered.

presentation_stages.narrative: A 26-year-old woman presents with 24 hours of abdominal pain. It began as a vague periumbilical ache, and over about six hours migrated to the right iliac fossa, where it is now constant and worse with movement and coughing. She has eaten nothing since the pain began (anorexia) and vomited once, after the pain started. Vitals (case data): temperature 37.6 C, heart rate 98/min, blood pressure 118/72 mmHg, respiratory rate 14/min, SpO2 99% on room air. Examination (case data): maximal tenderness at McBurney's point with light rebound tenderness; no rigidity and no generalised guarding; no costovertebral angle tenderness; bimanual examination finds no cervical motion tenderness, no adnexal tenderness and no mass. She reports no urinary symptoms and no vaginal discharge. Her last menstrual period was 3 weeks ago; she is sexually active and uses no hormonal contraception. The learner must now commit a stage-1 differential board before any test result exists.
presentation_stages.title: History, vitals, examination

presentation_stages.narrative: Bloods show a moderate inflammatory response: white cell count 12.4 x10^9/L with segmented neutrophils 78%, C-reactive protein 26 mg/L. Urinalysis is clear — no pyuria, no nitrites, no haematuria. The urine beta-hCG is NEGATIVE. Both appendicitis scores are now fully assessable: the Alvarado score totals 10 of 10 (very probable), while the Appendicitis Inflammatory Response score totals 6 of 12 (intermediate probability) — the two instruments place the same patient in different risk classes, and the stage-4 adjudication is built around that disagreement. The learner re-ranks the board.
presentation_stages.title: Laboratory and bedside tests

presentation_stages.narrative: Pelvic and transabdominal ultrasound: the appendix is not visualised (a non-result, recorded as such — non-visualisation is not a negative examination). Both ovaries are normal in size and appearance with preserved arterial and venous Doppler flow; there is no adnexal mass and no free fluid in the pouch of Douglas or elsewhere. The gynaecological must-not-miss hypotheses lose their imaging legs; the appendix question is untouched. The learner re-ranks the board and decides the next step.
presentation_stages.title: Ultrasound

presentation_stages.narrative: CT abdomen and pelvis with intravenous contrast: the appendix is dilated at 11 mm with wall thickening, periappendiceal fat stranding and an appendicolith — acute appendicitis. It arises from the caecal pole in standard position in the right iliac fossa. There is no perforation, no abscess, no free gas and no generalised contamination: uncomplicated appendicitis. The adnexa are unremarkable; there is no ureteric calculus and no hydronephrosis. The adjudication block evaluates both scores mechanically from the staged evidence, lists what excludes each rival, and hands the patient to the Theatre for laparoscopic appendicectomy in the procedure's standard configuration.
presentation_stages.title: CT, adjudication, disposition

review.required: Review of this case's clinical content (presentation, score application, LR use, differential weighting, disposition) by a qualified clinician before the case is used as validated teaching content.

case.synthetic_note: SYNTHETIC CASE. The patient is an authored fiction built for teaching; no real patient data exists in this module (design/07, master plan section 8 rule 9: education-only scope). Clinical facts the case relies on (score items and bands, likelihood ratios, reference ranges, test characteristics) are cited to sources consulted in-session in cases/parameters.json; the patient's particulars (age, values, findings) are case data and are labelled 'case data' wherever they appear.
